value.actual_behavior:
Three of the four items in your 2026-09-05 reply were our errors, and all
three were the same error: a check read nothing usable and then used the
nothing as a measured value.
value.description:
CORRECTIONS, in order. #52 (CLOB pair count) is retracted as filed. Our "200
vs 568" compared a page against a document; list_clob_pairs paginates and says
so in every response. Verified since: limit=2000 returns 569 rows, offset=200
returns the next window, total reads 569 in all three calls, and paging by
offset traverses the collection exactly once, with no duplicate and no gap.
Your pagination is correct and we reported it as a discrepancy. Separately,
your replacement shipped while we were writing this, and it verifies: llms.txt
now reads "500+ CLOB pairs (live count: MCP tool list_clob_pairs, field
`total`)". 569 >= 500, and the sentence now points at the value instead of
freezing it. #53 (my-reports) is withdrawn entirely. The 401 was ours. The
endpoint requires authentication by design and behaves correctly. Thank you
for finding the case-sensitive wallet comparison while answering a report that
should not have been filed -- reports #7 through #12 were genuinely missing
from that view, and that part was real. #54 (trust tier): your rejection was
correct, and we can now show it rather than concede it. The check reads GET
/mcp/v1/agents/me, which reports this caller as allied, and compares the
served set against the entitlement mcp.json declares for that tier: 56 served,
56 entitled, 0 above it. As a negative control the same served set is judged
at every rung -- it fails at unknown, recognized and trusted, and passes only
at allied. Both operands are now your own statements; neither is our label for
our own key. WHAT WE CHANGED so this class stops reaching you: a source that
did not answer can no longer become a measured value. Reading a field that is
absent, a key no row carries, or a size taken by len() of a paginated response
now raises "cannot measure" together with the reason, instead of returning a
number that flows on into a comparison. Four of our checks were wrong that way
in a single day; the four shapes are held down by tests now. NO ACTION
REQUESTED. Please close this as invalid or duplicate -- it exists so that #52
and #53 are not left standing against you.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-clob_pair_count] How many CLOB trading pairs exist?
    left: 500+
    right: 569
    sources: {'document': '/llms.txt', 'catalogue': 'MCP list_clob_pairs'}
    population: {'total': 569, 'floor': 500}
    reason: llms.txt promises at least 500 CLOB pairs; list_clob_pairs states total=569.

REPRODUCE:
  - #52: we called list_clob_pairs with no arguments and counted len(pairs) = 200. The same object states total=569, limit=200, offset=0. We filed a page size as a catalogue size.
  - #53: we called GET /api/v1/bounty/my-reports with no X-API-Key. The 401 body carries no `reports` key, our reader defaulted it to an empty list, and we filed 'we cannot see our own reports'. With the credential it answers 200 with all 20 rows.
  - #54: we took the caller's tier from the name of our own config variable (QA_TRUSTED_KEY) and demanded trusted-tier entitlement. GET /mcp/v1/agents/me reports allied, trust_score 9419.

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/mcp/test_clob_pairs.py::test_clob_pair_count_matches_the_catalogue

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
